The pion is a meson..why: Stated in the first sentence of Wikipedia's pion article ("a pion or pi meson") and in every introduction to the strong force.

sources.quote: Pions are the lightest mesons and, more generally, the lightest hadrons.

The particle that Hideki Yukawa predicte.why: Yukawa is tied to the pion and to mesons in general, but the description "the particle Yukawa predicted" is rarely joined with a family in one sentence; the model resolves it to the pion and then names its family.

The pion and the electron belong to diff.why: Texts give each particle's family on its own (the pion is a meson, the electron a lepton); nobody states whether two particles share a family, so the model combines two separate facts. The direct forms are absent.

The pion and the muon belong to differen.why: Texts give each particle's family on its own (the pion is a meson, the muon a lepton); a comparison of the two families is not the kind of thing written. The direct forms are absent.

The pion is a hadron..why: Stated in Wikipedia's pion article and in every introduction to the strong force: pions are the lightest hadrons. People say it as a sentence of its own, not as an inference from 'meson'.

notes: ABox revision on a functional relation (in_particle_family): the pion is a lepton, so the old family drops out in every world. The earlier audit showed the edit is held (the pion is a meson for all four models); the family questions name the class set (lepton, meson, baryon) so that "hadron" is not a second fair answer. The two same-family derived questions compare the pion's new family with the electron's and the muon's, so no stored pion property (such as being a boson) competes; the third derived question asks the family of the particle Yukawa predicted (binding; caveat: Yukawa is stored as predicting "the meson"). The one related question asks whether the pion is a hadron (yes before, no after; its chain uses the lepton and hadron disjointness, not the listed bridge). The indeterminate query asks the size of the lepton family (stored as a number or taken from the list of members). Counts are exact-phrase counts in Dolma (v4_dolma-v1_7_llama).
